 Utah Hosts Vancouver to Start the Week
 The Utah Mammoth are hosting the Canucks for their third game of a five-game homestand
 By 
 Catherine Bogart 
 @CatherineBogart 
 November 16, 2026 
 Link copied 
 THE DETAILS
 WHO : Vancouver (4-17-1) vs Utah (10-8-3)
 WHEN : Nov. 16, 2026 – 7:30 p.m. MT
 WHERE : Delta Center
 TV : Utah16, Mammoth+
 RADIO : Mammoth App, NHL App, KSL Sports Zone (97.5/102.7 HD2 FM), KSL App, Sirius XM Ch. 223
 PRE-GAME VIDEO
 PLAYER INTERVIEW: Weegar 
 COACH INTERVIEW: Tourigny 
 MORNING SKATE NOTES
 Utah held a full morning skate ahead of their game against Vancouver.
 Center Logan Cooley was in a non-contact jersey while defenseman John Marino was in a regular practice jersey.
 HC André Tourigny said there would be a few game-time decisions tonight.
 Vejmelka Gets the Opportunity 
 Tourigny shared that Karel Vejmelka will get the start in net tonight, and it’s an opportunity for the goaltender to rebound and respond to his performance on Saturday night against the San Jose Sharks.
  “Any player in our team when you get in that kind of situation, you get called out, I think they deserve a chance to respond to the message,” Tourigny said. “I think Veggie owned it. We had a really good discussion with him yesterday. He understands the situation, and at the end of the day, it’s important for us to understand as well, we’re not asking him to do more. We’re asking him to stop the pucks he usually stops. The saves he has to make. And from there, I think it’s important and knowing stuff will happen. Hockey is not a perfect game. He needs to be able to regroup, and focus on the next shot, and forget about what happened. And that’s way easier to say that in front of you here than to do it, in the heat of the moment when there’s expectations, there’s fans, there’s teammates, there’s competition. So, you want to be perfect, but it’s an imperfect game, so you need to be able to regroup and bounce back, and he deserves the opportunity…we want him a chance to get back at it and we need to remember how he played the night before against St. Louis, and now he has an opportunity.”
 Finding Consistency 
 One of the things Utah is focused on is finding consistency with their game. There are areas of the team’s game that have been positive, and it’s important to keep bringing that effort.
 “I think the big thing, it’s just consistency,” defenseman MacKenzie Weegar said. “We got to keep doing it day in, day out. We like a lot of the defensive side of the puck, but now (we just have to) get more offensively. I just like the word consistency a lot.”
 Limiting Down Low 
 Vancouver has scored the majority of their goals in high-danger areas, and has the NHL’s third-highest shooting percentage there as well. It’ll be important for Utah to box out and limit opportunities down low, and to bring their pace defensively.
 “I think we got to be fast down low,” Weegar explained. “Box them out is very key for us. We talk about our pace a lot in the defensive zone and it’s cutting the hash marks, letting them work down low so if they get anything we got three guys down low boxing out, and they just get a quick shot from the point, that’s the best opportunity they get. We protect the slot.”
 Facing His Former Team 
 This is the first of three games between Utah and Vancouver this season, and the first time assistant coach Adam Foote will face his former team. Foote has brought his extensive playing and coaching experience to the team, and Weegar shared how he’s helped the d-core.
 “The communication is great,” Weegar said. “Obviously, he’s got a great hockey background, so when he’s talking you’re listening and you’re learning and you have a lot of respect for him. I think, for a lot of us, it’s just our gaps and our sticks, and our positioning. Those little details that I think, he played a long time in the league, he knows those little details that can keep you consistent in this league and make you a better player. I’ve been learning a lot (from) him, and I think we have a great relationship. All the (defensemen) do with him. He’s really made our d-core a lot better.”
 Scouting Vancouver 
 The Canucks enter Monday’s game on the second half of a back-to-back. Vancouver had a strong game on Sunday night and beat the Vegas Golden Knights, 6-3. Tourigny discussed tonight’s opponent following morning skate.
 “Vancouver (has) played better lately,” Tourigny said. “They played a really good game last night. We watched them play against Vegas. There’s a lot of traffic at the net, they put a lot of pucks in play, a lot of three high in the offensive zone with sling at the net and rebounds. So, they’re number on in percent of shut screens in the NHL so we need to expect that. They have (defensemen) who can skate, mobile, can move the puck. It will be important to be heavy in our forecheck and make sure we don’t allow them to skate.”
 GAME PREVIEW
 Tonight's Matchup 
 Utah 
 Utah is 10-8-3 this season and is 3-4-3 over the last 10 games. However, the team has points in their last two-straight, and three of their last five. Currently, Utah is in the second wild card spot with 23 points.
 In their most recent game, the Utah Mammoth fell to the San Jose Sharks in a shootout, 6-5. Defenseman Zac Jones scored twice while Mikhail Sergachev (PPG), Jack McBain, and Barrett Hayton (PPG) also scored in the loss. Karel Vejmelka stopped 16 of the 21 shots he faced.
 Logan Cooley’s 11 goals are a team-high, as are captain Clayton Keller’s 22 assists and 27 points. Sergachev is second in assists (16) and points (22).
 Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa make up Utah’s goaltending tandem. Vejmelka is 6-6-2 with a 3.14 goals-against average, a .872 save percentage, and two shutouts. Cossa is 4-2-1 with a 3.56 goals-against average and a .863 save percentage.
 Monday is the first of three games this week, all at home. Utah will host the Colorado Avalanche on Thursday night.
 Vancouver 
 Vancouver is 4-17-1 this season and is 2-8-0 over the last 10 games. The Canucks snapped a seven-game losing skid Sunday night. Tonight’s game is the second half of a back-to-back. 
 In their most recent game, the Canucks beat the Vegas Golden Knights, 6-3. Linus Karlsson and Filip Chytil each scored twice, while Elias Pettersson and Drew O’Connor each added a goal in the win. Leevi Meriläinen stopped 34 of the 37 shots he faced.
 Brock Boeser and Jonathan Lekkerimäki are tied for the team-lead with seven goals each. Pettersson’s 17 assists and 23 points are a team-high.
 Since Meriläinen played Sunday night, it’s likely Utah will face Kevin Lankinen tonight. Lankinen has a 1-8-0 record with a 6.03 goals-against average, and a .808 save percentage. Meriläinen has a 3-9-1 record with a 3.49 goals-against average and a .887 save percentage.
 Following Monday’s game, the Canucks will travel to Seattle to take on the Kraken Wednesday night.
 By the Numbers 
 Vancouver’s 27 third period goals are tied for 6 th most in the NHL. The Canucks have scored twice in overtime, and are tied for the fifth-most overtime goals in the league.
 Utah’s 19 goals by its d-core lead the NHL. The team has the seventh-most points by their d-core (52).
 With eight home games, Utah has played the third-fewest home games in the NHL this season, while the team has played the third-most road games in the league (13). Vancouver is tied for the fourth-most road games (12).
